---
title: "Billboard Top 100"
author: Angel Legrand
format: html
execute:
  echo: false
---

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
billboard <- read_csv("data/billboard.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

The week columns are reshaped into `week` and `rank`, keeping the artist and
track columns to identify each song.

```{r}
billboard_long <- billboard |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("wk"),
    names_to = "week",
    names_prefix = "wk",
    names_transform = list(week = as.integer),
    values_to = "rank"
  )

billboard_long |>
  filter(!is.na(rank)) |>
  group_by(artist, track) |>
  summarise(
    last_week = max(week),
    last_rank = rank[which.max(week)],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(last_week == 20) |>
  summarise(
    Songs = n(),
    Ranked_below_50 = sum(last_rank > 50),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

Summarize each song's first rank, best rank, first week at its best rank, and
total weeks on the chart. The three highlighted songs are the earliest and
latest to reach number one, and the top-10 song with the longest chart run.

```{r}
song_summary <- billboard_long |>
  filter(!is.na(rank)) |>
  arrange(week) |>
  group_by(artist, track) |>
  summarise(
    first_rank = first(rank),
    best_rank = min(rank),
    first_week_at_best = min(week[rank == min(rank)]),
    total_weeks = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

notable_top_10 <- bind_rows(
  song_summary |>
    filter(best_rank == 1) |>
    slice_min(first_week_at_best, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    mutate(trajectory = "Fastest to number one"),
  song_summary |>
    filter(best_rank == 1) |>
    slice_max(first_week_at_best, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    mutate(trajectory = "Slowest to number one"),
  song_summary |>
    filter(best_rank <= 10) |>
    slice_max(total_weeks, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    mutate(trajectory = "Longest top-10 chart run")
) |>
  select(trajectory, artist, track, first_rank, best_rank,
         first_week_at_best, total_weeks)

notable_top_10 |>
  knitr::kable()
```

These three lines show the selected songs' rankings over their chart runs.

```{r}
top_10_long <- billboard_long |>
  inner_join(
    song_summary |>
      filter(best_rank <= 10) |>
      select(artist, track),
    by = c("artist", "track")
  )

highlighted_songs <- notable_top_10 |>
  distinct(artist, track) |>
  mutate(song_name = paste(track, artist, sep = " — "))

highlighted_long <- top_10_long |>
  inner_join(
    highlighted_songs,
    by = c("artist", "track")
  )

ggplot(top_10_long, aes(x = week, y = rank,
                        group = interaction(artist, track))) +
  geom_line(color = "gray75", alpha = 0.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_line(
    data = highlighted_long,
    aes(color = song_name),
    linewidth = 1,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  labs(
    title = "Top-10 Song Trajectories",
    x = "Week on chart",
    y = "Chart rank (1 is highest)",
    color = "Notable songs"
  )
```

This histogram shows the distribution of Billboard chart positions in week 1.

```{r}
ggplot(billboard, aes(x = wk1)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 10, boundary = 0) +
  labs(
    title = "Billboard Chart Positions in Week 1",
    x = "Chart position",
    y = "Number of songs",
    subtitle = paste("Number of values:", sum(!is.na(billboard$wk1)))
  )
```

This table counts the missing and present rankings for each selected week.

```{r}
billboard |>
  select(wk1, wk4, wk10, wk20, wk40, wk76) |>
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "Week",
    values_to = "Ranking"
  ) |>
  group_by(Week) |>
  summarise(
    Missing = sum(is.na(Ranking)),
    Present = sum(!is.na(Ranking)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(Week = factor(Week, levels = c("wk1", "wk4", "wk10", "wk20", "wk40", "wk76"))) |>
  arrange(Week) |>
  mutate(Week = as.character(Week)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

Each line shows a song's ranking across the weeks it appeared on the chart.

```{r}
ggplot(
  billboard_long,
  aes(x = week, y = rank, group = interaction(artist, track))
) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.2, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  labs(
    title = "Billboard Song Rankings Over Time",
    x = "Week on chart",
    y = "Chart rank (1 is highest)"
  )
```
